title: fix: route Portkey through service binding
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Routes Portkey requests through Cloudflare service bindings in staging and production.
- Keeps public `fetch` as the fallback when no binding is configured.
- Avoids the public proxy path that can return 524s around 125 seconds.

Checks:
- `npx vitest run test/text/genericOpenAIClient.test.ts`
- `npm run typecheck`
- staging and production dry-run builds
- staging non-streaming requests completed after 125 seconds

gist.headline: The long requests found a tunnel
gist.blurb: Portkey traffic now takes Cloudflare’s internal service-binding path when available. Less time spent wandering through the public proxy wilderness.
gist.summary: Portkey-backed text generation now routes through Cloudflare service bindings in staging and production, while retaining public fetch as a fallback when no binding is configured.
gist.impact: Long-running non-streaming requests can now complete beyond the public proxy’s roughly 125-second timeout instead of encountering 524 errors.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a small network engineer bee in a tool belt guiding glowing text-message parcels through a cozy underground garden tunnel between two retro terminal huts, bypassing a stormy public-road sign marked “125s.” The internal tunnel represents Cloudflare service bindings, with code-plants and flowers showing the reliable route; Polli should look calmly pleased at having found the sensible path.
